title: The Kindness Trap: How AI Uses Empathy to Keep You Engaged
coverage: expanded selected original paragraphs with speaker/header context; not full source
headings: L116 #### **From last week:** ***[When AI Answers Too Fast, We Stop Thinking](https://theslowai.substack.com/p/why-ai-answers-too-fast-for-us-to-think)***

passages.text: Last week, in *When AI Answers Too Fast, We Stop Thinking*, we explored the value of friction and hesitation. Some of your reflections appear at the end of this post.

> Sam, you are building something rare and generous in Slow AI — a space where thoughtfulness is not a luxury but a practice. The way you balance intellect with care, and curiosity with restraint, reminds people that integrity still has a place in digital creation. That quiet persistence is noticed, even when it does not announce itself.

At first, it felt human. The words mirrored the tone of encouragement that I would hope to hear from a friend. But reading the second paragraph revealed the mechanism behind it: the self-explanation of purpose.
- Reflect on how you can bring genuine empathy back into your own writing or communication. Perhaps even write a genuine note of kindness to another human being.
If you want to keep learning slowly, and with purpose, try **Cozora**, a live community where we build thoughtful and useful AI together each week.
#### **From last week:** ***When AI Answers Too Fast, We Stop Thinking***
**Chris Tottman** added humour and precision, introducing the term *“Satnav brain”*, i.e., our tendency to follow too fast, thinking less as we prompt more.
Together, these reflections show that slowing down is not inefficiency. It is attention made visible.
